top_cluster.headline: President Trump signed an executive order revising the CDC-recommended childhood vaccine schedule — cutting the recommended vaccine count and directing the MMR shot be split into three separate doses — while separately, GOP senators released private Fauci text messages about COVID vaccines and pregnancy, and Trump denied discussing a Fauci prosecution with DOJ officials.
top_cluster.left_framing: Left and center-left outlets frame the vaccine order as a dangerous, unscientific overreach that endangers children, leaning heavily on condemnation from doctors, medical associations, and lawmakers, and linking it to previously debunked vaccine-autism claims and past legal pushback. On Fauci, left coverage frames the text release as a GOP-driven disclosure/scrutiny exercise focused on process rather than assessing the substance of the medical claims.
top_cluster.center_framing: Center outlets (Axios, PBS, The Hill) report the executive order's contents relatively straightforwardly, sourcing the White House fact sheet while also giving voice to medical-authority criticism (AMA, AAP) without strong editorializing. On Fauci, The Hill neutrally reports Trump's denial of discussing prosecution, framing it as distancing rather than confirmation of an investigation.
top_cluster.right_framing: Right and far-right outlets frame the vaccine order as a courageous restoration of parental choice and 'common sense,' aligning the U.S. with other developed nations and casting establishment/media resistance as suspicious. On Fauci, they frame the released texts as proof of official deception — that Fauci privately knew of miscarriage risks tied to COVID vaccination while public messaging downplayed or mandated it — and push for continued accountability, including contempt proceedings and scrutiny of China's role.
top_cluster.left_omissions: Left coverage largely omits the specific substantive content of Fauci's texts (the cytokine-storm/miscarriage warning details) and the accountability push tied to a Senate contempt vote, focusing instead on the political mechanics of the text release rather than engaging with the claims themselves.
top_cluster.right_omissions: Right coverage largely omits the extent and authority of medical-community condemnation (AMA's 'risk to children's health,' AAP's 'dangerous' characterization) and the context that U.S. measles cases are at a 35-year high, as well as the disputed legal question of whether the order oversteps CDC authority and revives discredited vaccine-autism claims.

blindspot_narrative: Left-leaning outlets are avoiding the DOJ's Duke Law affirmative-action enforcement story entirely, leaving an active civil-rights allegation uncontested by any left-of-center account. Right-leaning outlets are avoiding Todd Blanche's own confirmation controversy and giving almost no attention to the 9th Circuit's Meta/TikTok liability ruling, an outcome that cuts awkwardly against both pro-business and anti-Big-Tech instincts on the right. Both sides continue to skip substantive legal analysis of the Mamdani tax case, preferring political framing over the actual litigation merits — consistent with last cycle's pattern of surface-level coverage on ongoing court fights.
